units.translation: 446 ⟦1⟧ with accusative as at ⟦2⟧ 409. The tribrach ⟦3⟧- (or the dactyl -⟦4⟧) is one of the few non-necessary ones in Aeschylus (like ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧).

V. 447 is, perhaps not without intention, echoing 445: ⟦1⟧ – ⟦2⟧. – (448) That the not yet purified murderer was not allowed to address anyone, precisely so as not to defile them with his guilt, was also indicated at 276 ff.; the scholiast quotes from Euripides (Frg. 996 N) ⟦3⟧; ⟦4⟧; see also ⟦5⟧, of Jason and Medea, who, defiled by the murder of Apsyrtus, turn to Circe: ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧. In Euripides, without regard to the purification that has taken place, the behavior of the others toward Orestes remains so until he is acquitted, Iph. T. 949 ff. (951 ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧; cf. Orest. 75). Also Telephus came in Aeschylus's ⟦11⟧ as blood-defiled and therefore ⟦12⟧ to Mysia, Aristot. Poet. c. 24 (criticized as ⟦13⟧), comic poet in Ath. VI, 224E. X, 421D (Frg. 144 Ddf.).
I will take away the great care of your words
I will tell you a great proof of these things
They two, speechless and voiceless, rushed to the hearth and sat
as is the custom for wretched suppliants
In silence they made me speechless
so that I might be without their feast and drink
⟦1⟧ (as at 166. 254 and often) would be clearer, and is perhaps what Aeschylus wrote.
⟦1⟧ is of course intentional (like ⟦2⟧.. ⟦3⟧ 281 ff.); this is exactly the Heraclitean ⟦4⟧ (⟦5⟧) ⟦6⟧ (on ⟦7⟧).
